rows.accountTerms: Local silicon on bare-cedar-fog, no signup and no real key needed (any non-empty value satisfies the adapter's bearer header; Ollama ignores it). Serves gemma3, phi4-mini, qwen3, qwen2.5, llama3.2 locally.
rows.note: Verified 2026-08-31 live: dispatched a real chat completion to qwen3:1.7b through this same generic adapter and received a genuine answer (19 input / 1966 output tokens, ~161s wall time -- qwen3 emits its own chain-of-thought before the final content). Runs through Ollama's native /api/chat with thinking off (2026-09-24), so reasoning models such as qwen3 answer in content instead of returning reasoning only. 2026-10-04 measured: llama3.2:3b and qwen3:1.7b both returned correct strict json_schema through /v1/chat/completions (20s and 79s on this machine's CPU); the installed set is only these two, so llama3.2:3b is the single pin shared by admission and catalog default. The schema reaches Ollama's native /api/chat as `format`. Allowance: this machine's one inference engine, capacity 1.

rows.accountTerms: Free tier, no card required. Model roster rotates; as of 2026-08-31 it serves openai/gpt-oss-20b, openai/gpt-oss-120b, qwen/qwen3.8-27b, groq/compound, allam-2-7b and others (query GET /openai/v1/models for the live list) rather than the Llama-3.x ids earlier trackers named. Limits are per-organization and per-model.
rows.note: Verified 2026-08-31 live through this adapter's CLI: model llama-3.1-8b-instant (the value carried in an earlier draft of this row) no longer exists on this account. Listed live models via an authenticated GET to /openai/v1/models and retried with openai/gpt-oss-20b, which answered a real one-line completion ("pong", 78 prompt / 36 completion tokens -- the model spends some completion budget on internal reasoning before the final content, so a caller should budget max-tokens generously -- ~0.6s wall time). apiKeyEnvVar corrected from the placeholder GROQ_API_KEY to the house .env's actual name, API_KEY_GROQ. 2026-10-04 measured: /models serves gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b, qwen3.8-27b; all three returned correct strict json_schema (gpt-oss-120b 1.1s, qwen3.8-27b 0.7s, gpt-oss-20b 0.5s). Pinned gpt-oss-120b, the strongest. Allowance read from this key's response headers for gpt-oss-120b: x-ratelimit-limit-tokens 8000 per minute, x-ratelimit-limit-requests 1000 per day (rolling; reset-requests read 1m26s after one call). The earlier 60s minimum interval, 6000 TPM and 900-token output ceiling were unmeasured self-limits and are removed or raised to the measured allowance; capacity 4 = 8000 tokens/minute divided by a 2000-token bounded lot.

rows.note: Corrected 2026-09-03 from the census at /tmp/.../free-compute-lanes-census.md (source: inference-docs.cerebras.ai/support/rate-limits, WebFetched). rows.note: Checked 2026-08-31: no credential exists anywhere in the house .env for this provider -- confirmed the same way as the cerebras row (variable-name diff only, no content read). Neither MISTRAL_API_KEY nor a house-prefixed API_KEY_MISTRAL variant is present. A live dispatch attempt through this adapter's CLI fails before any network call: "MISTRAL_API_KEY is not set for provider mistral". rows.accountTerms: OpenRouter's first-party Free Variant guide states that :free variants provide access without cost. Its Free Models Router guide also states that requests routed to free models have no charge. A live authenticated GET /api/v1/models on 2026-09-07 returned this exact model with prompt and completion prices both 0; a bounded chat completion then returned ordinary content.
rows.note: Verified 2026-09-07 live through the shared receiver-owned OpenAI-compatible adapter: a 12-prompt-token, 55-completion-token bounded request completed in about 0.87 s with ordinary completion content. Provider availability remains quota-bound and must fail closed on rate limit or refusal. 2026-10-04 measured: /api/v1/models lists nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free at prompt and completion price 0, advertising structured_outputs and response_format (cohere/north-mini-code:free advertises neither). Allowance: 50 requests/day across all :free models (X-RateLimit-Limit 50, error code free-models-per-day; the key holds 0 credits, usage 0), which was already exhausted when this session first called (HTTP 429 on first request), so no live strict-schema call was possible; resets with the provider's daily window (UTC). The same model returned correct strict json_schema on NVIDIA NIM (2.7s). Capacity 1 follows the 50 requests/day allowance. Re-verify with one call after the window resets. Machine-readable zero-cash admission added 2026-10-10: this exact :free model is contractually no-charge; paid overage is forbidden by selecting only the :free slug.

rows.accountTerms: 20+ models with a :free model-id suffix at $0/token. 20 requests/minute; 50 requests/day with a $0 balance, rising to 1,000 requests/day after a one-time $10 credit purchase. The free-model roster rotates fast enough that a hardcoded model id goes stale within weeks -- query GET /api/v1/models and filter for an id ending :free before dispatching.
rows.note: 2026-09-12 read-only admission: free-account check passed; the live catalog no longer lists minimax/minimax-m3:free. Default now cohere/north-mini-code:free, which the live catalog reports as zero-priced with tools support. This catalog observation does not guarantee request capacity. Prior observations: Verified 2026-08-31 live through this adapter's CLI: two of three previously-plausible :free model ids were already gone or shared-pool rate-limited (meta-llama/llama-3.2-3b-instruct:free returned HTTP 404 telling the caller to use the paid slug instead; google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free returned a real HTTP 429 "temporarily rate-limited upstream" against OpenRouter's shared free pool -- a genuine, live observed-exhausted result for that specific model, distinct from the credential itself). minimax/minimax-m3:free then answered a real one-line completion ("pong", 170 prompt / 2 completion tokens, ~10.2s wall time, $0 cost). apiKeyEnvVar corrected from the placeholder OPENROUTER_API_KEY to the house .env's actual name, API_KEY_OPENROUTER. Because individual :free models rotate and rate-limit independently of the account, a caller should treat a single model's 429 as that model's exhaustion, not the provider's, and retry a different :free id from the live /models listing before concluding OpenRouter itself is exhausted -- see the openrouter-poolside, openrouter-glm and openrouter-nemotron rows, added 2026-09-03 as exactly that: additional :free rotation targets on the same account and key.

NVIDIA build API developer access. The engine binds the exact observed model and forbids paid overage. 2026-10-04 measured (one probe per model, strict json_schema, 10-minute deadline): nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b PASS 2.7s; nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b PASS 2.7s; glm-5.3-flash PASS 250s; kimi-k3 PASS 13s on one call but returned degenerate reasoning-only output with null content on a later call; openai/gpt-oss-20b PASS 1.6s; deepseek-v4.1-flash returned gateway 504 at 303s (provider-side; retest later); meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct (the old pin) returned 200 with non-conforming JSON. Pinned nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b, the largest model that conforms reliably; latency is a measured fact, not a selection criterion. Allowance: the account's NVIDIA build API credit allowance (no card on file; paidOverage forbidden); per-minute request limit not read, capacity 4 retained from the prior admission.
Provider execution and credential reference data consolidated from the former provider package. Not in the routing order.

rows.accountTerms: 10,000 neurons per day on the account. The account is on the Cloudflare Free plan (subscriptions read 2026-09-24), where Workers AI stops at the daily allocation instead of billing overage.
rows.note: Verified 2026-09-24 live: llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct answered through the OpenAI-compatible /ai/v1/chat/completions surface. The account id is read from CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID. 2026-10-04 measured: @cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b (2.0s) and @cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast (1.5s) both returned correct strict json_schema; pinned gpt-oss-120b, the strongest. Allowance: 10,000 neurons/day on the Workers Free plan, which stops at the limit and never bills; resets at 00:00 UTC. At published rates (gpt-oss-120b 31,000 neurons per million input tokens, 69,000 per million output tokens) a 2000-token lot is about 100 neurons, so about 100 lots/day; capacity 2.

Verified key and model listing; the engine renews a short credential-bound no-overage lease before use. 2026-10-04 measured: gemini-2.5-flash and 2.5-flash-lite return 404 'no longer available to new users'; gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-3.1-flash-lite and gemma-4-31b-it each returned correct strict json_schema via the OpenAI-compatible surface (gemini-3.8-flash 3.7s end to end, gemma-4-31b-it 43s). ai.google.dev/pricing lists gemini-3.8-flash input and output (including thinking) as 'Free of charge' for the no-billing tier. Per-minute and per-day request quotas are not exposed by the API and were not measured; capacity 2 is a conservative placeholder until they are read from AI Studio. gemini-3.5/3.7/flash-latest answered 503 demand spikes.

Claude Code in print mode on the local login: text completion with no tools, MCP servers or settings; optional provider-validated JSON output via params.outputSchema. One live claude process at a time; a second request is refused at once rather than queued.

Codex exec on the local ChatGPT login (CODEX_HOME), read-only sandbox in a fresh directory, allowlisted environment; params.webSearch enables live web search and the completion's raw carries completedSearches. Reached through dispatchInOrder's prefer, outside the routing order.

Antigravity CLI print mode on the Google AI Pro login (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli; signed in 2026-10-02, interaction-data collection off). The subscription's weekly compute cap is its meter; a turn refused on it settles as antigravity-weekly-compute-exhausted. Models from `agy models`: gemini-3.8/3.7/3.6-flash-{high,medium,low}, gemini-3.1-pro-{high,low}, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-6-thinking, gpt-oss-120b-medium. Sandboxed in a fresh directory, allowlisted environment, no tool permission granted; optional provider-validated JSON output via params.outputSchema. Reached through dispatchInOrder's prefer, outside the routing order. Gemini CLI's personal login no longer serves this plan (Google moved it to Antigravity CLI, 2026-06-18).

routingPolicy.rule: Try the armed providers in `order`; when one fails (rate limit, capacity, HTTP error, missing model, empty answer) pass the packet to the next. What each call consumed is measured from its own response: token usage, the provider's reported cost, and its rate-limit headers. A row asserts no cost.
